doc.name: A — cold brew catalogue, travel context, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: canned nitro cold brew
Category: cold brew
Shot programme: travel context
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a cold brew catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the top-down flat in a travel context treatment.

SUBJECT. A canned nitro cold brew. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Directly overhead, product and props arranged on a single plane. Shoot on a 100mm macro at f/4, framing for a tight crop that breaks the subject at the frame edge.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with tungsten practicals in frame carrying the warm layer. Stage the product on or against raw board-formed concrete, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward Eterna-style muted greens with gentle highlight roll-off. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

SUBJECT. A canned nitro cold brew. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Product in its real use environment with lived-in supporting props. Shoot on a 40mm anamorphic at f/2.8, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with split gel lighting, teal on the shadow side and magenta on the key side. Stage the product on or against hand-thrown ceramic, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a cinematic grade with a warm key and green-leaning ambient shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.
